competences: The learner recalls the meaning and purposes of community by-laws.
The learner identifies political leaders and council officers involved in local government.
languageCompetence: Reads and spells by-laws, village council, political leader, chairperson, councillor and election.
objectives: By the end of the period learners should recall at least three purposes of by-laws.
By the end of the period learners should answer original questions on political and local-council leaders.
priorKnowledge: Learners studied the meaning, importance and local-council duties connected with by-laws in the previous period.
materials: P4 Social Studies reference exercise on local councils
references: P4 Social Studies Notes for Terms 1–3

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the meaning and importance of by-laws and asks "What title is given to the political head of a village?". They explain that today's Part B practises recognising the local leaders who carry out community rules.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall yesterday's work on by-laws, name village council positions and give short answers to the starter question.

steps.content: By-laws are local laws made by local councils. They help local councils settle community disputes. They promote peace, security and order. They promote respect for people's rights. Village councils protect people and their property. Village councils promote sanitation and unity. Ignorance may hinder enforcement of local laws. Shortage of funds is a problem for district leaders.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the eight source-grounded revision points, beginning with "By-laws are local laws made by local councils." and "They help local councils settle community disputes.". They ask learners to relate the rules to council leadership and explain each local-government term.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the revision points, connect them with the role of local councils, explain new words and copy the notes.

steps.content: What title is given to the political head of a village? | How do political leaders attain leadership powers? | Apart from the chairperson, mention any three other members on the LC I executive committee. | Mention any four types of leaders. | Mention any three examples of political leaders.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the original source questions, including "How do political leaders attain leadership powers?" and "Apart from the chairperson, mention any three other members on the LC I executive committee.". They supervise written answers, mark the exercise and discuss corrections without inventing extra activities.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the supplied questions about political leaders, compare their answers with the revision notes and correct mistakes.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher checks the key facts about by-laws and elected councils by asking "Mention any four types of leaders." and "Mention any three examples of political leaders.". They confirm the positions learners should remember and assign revision.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners give brief oral answers, name the leaders who enforce local decisions and complete their written corrections.

assessment: Mark learners' answers to "What title is given to the political head of a village?", "Apart from the chairperson, mention any three other members on the LC I executive committee.", and "Mention any four types of leaders.". Check their answers against the documented local council facts.
homework: Answer the original question: "Mention any three examples of political leaders."
